### Problem

The maintainer cannot tell what waits on him without reading labels. One chain in DiluxOne/diluxone-fm (#274 → pull request #283) carried autopilot, autopilot:run-1, autopilot:waiting, autopilot:answered, layer:browser, repro:no-way, bug:unconfirmed, awaiting-acceptance and needs-human at once. labels.yml has 70 labels and the code makes more (`autopilot:run-N`, `free-N`, `round-N`); several are never used (`needs:maintainer`, `exists-in-pro`, `spike`, `by-design`, `review:full`, `claim:long`, `version:minor`). A Bug the maintainer writes himself goes through the outside reporter's triage and reproduction and gets `bug:unconfirmed` and `repro:no-way` (DiluxOne/diluxone-fm#274). "What waits" (#529) is rewritten once a day, lists only pull requests older than a day, leaves out issues waiting on a person (`needs-human`, an acceptance) and notifies nobody. And no autopilot pull request that changes what a user sees carries screenshots: the template's "📸 Screenshots" is always empty, and DiluxOne/diluxone-fm keeps Playwright's screenshots only on failure.

### Scope

- The board's state block, which the rest of this issue reads and writes.
- A Bug written by someone with the maintain or admin role is accepted with its writing and skips the outside reporter's triage and reproduction labels.
- One "what waits on me" view, updated on every event, with each action and its URL, that notifies the person (one mention) when something new waits on them, issues and pull requests alike.
- The bot's first comment on every new issue says what happens next and who waits: the triage, then a maintainer's acceptance, then the autopilot codes it in the organisation's runners; and that whoever wants to write the code themselves comments `/claim` (or ticks the form's box) before it is accepted. The README of this repository, of every repository (from `agents-block.md` and the README template) and CONTRIBUTING.md open with the same.
- Everything here works the same for an outside contributor on a public repository: the board says when something waits on them, they are mentioned once, and they are never asked for a maintainer's step.
- A pull request that touches the browser layer attaches before and after screenshots of the affected specs and fills its "📸 Screenshots" section.

### Out of scope

- Moving counters and intermediate steps off labels and removing the unused ones (about eight labels a person sees): its own issue, in steps, one at a time in the core (decided on #606).
- Comparing screenshots pixel by pixel.

### Acceptance criteria

- C2: Given a Bug opened by a maintainer, when it is triaged, then it gets neither `bug:unconfirmed` nor `repro:no-way`.
- C3: Given something that starts waiting on a person, when it does, then the "what waits on me" view lists it with the action and its URL within minutes and the person is notified once.
- C5: Given a new issue opened by an outside contributor, when the bot first comments, then it says that the autopilot will code it once accepted unless they `/claim` it, and its board later names whom it waits on, mentioning them when it is them.
- C4: Given an autopilot pull request that changes a browser-layer file, when it is marked ready, then its "📸 Screenshots" section links before and after images of the affected specs.

### Criticality

Normal
